author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Saudi Arabia temporarily shut its East-West oil pipeline as a precaution after a drone attack that officials in Baghdad and Riyadh said originated in Iraq. Responsibility for the strike was not immediately clear. The 1,200-kilometer system carries crude from eastern production areas to the Red Sea, giving the kingdom an export route that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz.

Reuters reported that tracking data and analyst estimates put recent pipeline flows at roughly 4 million to 5 million barrels a day, equal to about 4% to 5% of global oil supply. The closure therefore adds a new transportation risk at a time when regional conflict has already pressured maritime routes. No timetable for reopening was immediately announced.

The attack followed reports that Houthi forces had reached Perim Island at the mouth of the Bab el-Mandeb strait, another critical shipping passage. Iraq dismissed a military commander and closed a border crossing with Iran after the drone launches, while Saudi Arabia sought additional U.S. assistance. Washington offered intelligence support but not direct military action. The pipeline’s status and attribution for the attack remain developing.
dek: The kingdom temporarily closed the major Red Sea route as a precaution after officials said drones launched from Iraq struck the system.
headline: Saudi Arabia shuts East-West oil pipeline after drone attack
